claims.statement: The cloud mandate's source-defined contributor cohort includes publishing apps/actions, releases, high-importance contributions/admin roles, org owners with repos/users, package-repository contributors/admins and enterprise admins. Criteria may change; notification starts a 45-day enrollment window. Pinned eligibility prose is not current target selection evidence.

The platform mandate is separate from org/enterprise requirements, and one account's eligibility does not imply everyone else's. Enterprise managed and GHES users are excluded from this platform password-account program, not exempt from IdP or organizational security objectives.

After the 45-day setup plus seven-day grace expires, web access is blocked until enrollment. Existing PAT and OAuth tokens keep functioning and enrollment does not revoke them; locked accounts cannot create PATs or authorize new apps. Browser lockout does not certify token revocation or automation containment.

The guide recommends primary TOTP with passkey/security-key or Mobile backup, describing passkeys/keys as unsupported primary enrollment methods. This is an enrollment-path limitation, not denial of separately documented single-step passkey login; SMS reliability claims are qualified by threat-model risks.

Retaining the device-id cookie supports verified-device recovery, while daily clearing can prevent that factor. This is conditional recovery guidance, not permission to disable tracking protections globally or proof cookie presence authenticates rightful ownership.

The source recommends example TOTP providers and RFC6238 compatibility, and describes an 80-bit secret versus RFC HOTP's cited 128-bit recommendation while suggesting ignoring a FreeOTP warning. Preserve this weaker-parameter statement as platform-specific source evidence, not a general cryptographic policy or installation recommendation.

Selected password-account users still need platform 2FA even with organization SAML SSO+2FA because personal content/profile lie outside that SSO boundary. Initial and sensitive-action proof differs from corporate sessions; SSO login alone cannot pass personal-account mandate.

Email device verification is not 2FA because inbox access enables reset and device check. The second factor must be distinct from inbox; enrollment removes email login verification but does not prove recovery mailbox security.

Selected bots/shared service accounts must enroll without changing existing tokens. Secure shared TOTP storage is a source recommendation, requiring accountable credential custody and approval, not permission to expose secrets or substitute shared storage for access auditing.
Mandatory 2FA does not require a phone number unless SMS is chosen. Unsupported regions use TOTP; capability limits cannot compel personal phone disclosure or waive the authentication objective.

The SMS list is FPT/GHEC-only, based on delivery reliability and periodically updated. Every region entry was reviewed as a pinned capability list, not legal jurisdiction, current live coverage or guarantee of delivery; absence leads to TOTP rather than an exemption.

The list includes alternate/overlapping geographic labels such as Aland Islands and Finland/Aland Islands. Exact source labels require normalization with preserved provenance before operational matching; one similar country label cannot prove phone-route compatibility.

The 2FA index spans FPT/GHES/GHEC and lists ten children. Its phone-code/password intro is narrower than passkey and secondary-key alternatives; cloud mandatory feature note cannot establish GHES or IdP applicability. Navigation and receipts do not prove enforcement.

TOTP is locally generated from the enrolled secret, not sent by GitHub. Diagnose correct app/account, automatic clock/timezone, fresh thirty-second code and no extra characters before recovery. A failed code is not permission to read secrets or automatically reset methods.

Provider backup/export may restore TOTP after device loss, but varies by provider and needs authentic owner restore evidence. Merely locating an app or backup file cannot prove recovery or current seed.

Cloud SMS diagnosis checks receivable SMS/plan, possible carrier charges, filtering, coverage, restart and provider outage/delivery inquiry. Disabling filters, power cycling or disclosing phone/request time are owner-controlled device/provider actions, not silently authorized assessment steps.

GitHub status and carrier investigation can inform delivery incidents; the guide says cloud support cannot troubleshoot 2FA methods including SMS. Support warning does not contradict separate factor-based account recovery review or prove an outage exists now.
Preconfigured passkey/key or cloud Mobile may be used if troubleshooting fails; otherwise recovery applies. Availability must be observed, not inferred from a method once listed or device possession.

Recovery codes use one ten-alphanumeric-character code with a middle hyphen, are single-use, and previous sets invalidate on generation or disable/re-enable. Default filename is only a search clue; no device/password-manager search, secret capture or code testing is performed.
